text.p: These are the leading stories in the Zambian press on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- The Zambia Revenue Authority sacks 20 workers for corruption.
- East African Catholic sisters blame structural adjustment programmes for the falling life expectancy in many countries in sub-Saharan Africa.
- Finance minister Ronald Penza says government is capable of awarding public workers pay rises as agreed last year.
- Police in Lusaka blame increasing crime in the capital on the mass exodus of people from the northern Copperbelt Province.
